title: When four mean wind speeds reverse a turbine choice
abstract: We compare linearly interpolated, equally rated turbine power curves on a representative northern North Dakota resource at 80 m. Replacing 8,760 hourly speeds with four within-group means reverses 19 of 395 eligible pairwise rankings. The Fuhrlander FL 1500_70 and GE 1.5sle also reverse on a second, previously unevaluated Minnesota resource. Group means and supports yield sharp distributional bounds for the power difference. Mean speed and mean excesses above the differential curve's knots recover the hourly comparison exactly. These are common-inflow predictions rather than measurements of delivered power.
